narrationScript: To overcome the challenge of volatile data, we'll integrate a database into our Flask application. Specifically, we'll use SQLite. SQLite is an excellent choice for development and smaller applications because it's lightweight, self-contained, and file-based. This means it doesn't require a separate server process running in the background, making it incredibly easy to set up and manage. Now, to interact with our SQLite database from within our Python Flask application, we'll use a powerful tool called SQLAlchemy. SQLAlchemy is a Python SQL toolkit and, importantly, an Object Relational Mapper, or ORM. An ORM allows us to interact with our database using familiar Python objects and methods, instead of writing raw SQL queries. This makes our code much more Pythonic, readable, and generally easier to maintain. To seamlessly integrate SQLAlchemy with Flask, we'll use the Flask-SQLAlchemy extension, which handles much of the boilerplate setup for us.
deliveryNotes: Highlight 'Pythonic, readable, and easier to maintain'
